title: When hurt keeps asking to become your identity
issueStatement: Something real happened, but the mind has begun protecting the wound as if staying injured were the last honest thing left to do.
centralInsight: Gurbani does not ask you to call harm harmless. It asks you to stop letting bitterness govern the inner room. Forgiveness loosens fear, cleans speech, and makes peace livable again.
practicalReflection: Replay can feel like loyalty to the truth, but often it is pain asking for permanent residence. Forgiveness is the moment the soul stops kneeling to the injury.
actionPrompt: Name the hurt without reducing it, then ask what one act of release would look like if you no longer needed the wound to organize your identity.

daily.label: Daily
daily.title: Forgiveness in the repeating memory
daily.issueStatement: Most days the hurt returns not as drama but as a rehearsed sentence, a tightened body, or a way of re-reading ordinary events through the old injury.
daily.centralInsight: The Guru teaches forgiveness in the daily replay itself. Freedom begins where the memory stops being fed as faithfully as the wound once was.
daily.practicalReflection: Daily bitterness is often quiet, disciplined, and familiar. It can look like realism while steadily narrowing the heart.
daily.actionPrompt: When the familiar replay starts today, interrupt it with one line of prayer before the whole old script can finish.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: Forgiveness when you feel freshly provoked
pressure.issueStatement: Pressure and fresh offense make it feel naive to soften. The mind wants immediate retaliation, or at least the right to stay inwardly armed.
pressure.centralInsight: Under pressure, forgiveness is not passivity. It is the refusal to let a new spark light the whole stored fire again.
pressure.practicalReflection: Pressure makes old injuries recruit new moments. Gurbani keeps the present from being swallowed by that old flame.
pressure.actionPrompt: Before responding to the fresh offense, ask whether your next move belongs to truth or to accumulated grievance.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: Returning after bitterness has already ruled
repair.issueStatement: You already fed the resentment, replayed the injury, or spoke from the wound, and now you are left with both the original hurt and what bitterness has added to it.
repair.centralInsight: Repair begins when bitterness is confessed as bondage, not protected as discernment. The Guru opens return after the heart has hardened.
repair.practicalReflection: Forgiveness after the fact often starts with grieving what resentment has done to you, not only what others did first.
repair.actionPrompt: Tell the truth about how the grudge is shaping you now, then release one ritual of resentment you have been preserving.

practice.title: Practicing release before resentment matures
practice.issueStatement: Forgiveness usually fails long before the major moment. It fails in the small permissions given to replay, suspicion, and cherished grievance.
practice.centralInsight: The heart learns forgiveness through repeated release. The Guru trains you to loosen early, before the wound becomes architecture.
practice.practicalReflection: A forgiving life is not forgetful. It is disciplined about what it continues to feed.
practice.actionPrompt: Choose one resentment pattern to interrupt early this week and practice release there before it becomes your familiar shelter.
